svg.title: CausalLab: conditioning can block a chain or open a collider
svg.desc: Eight d-separation queries on four fixed DAG panels. A chain and common-cause fork connect X and Y, but conditioning on the middle node separates them. A collider is closed until it or its descendant is conditioned on. Removing incoming edges into X separates a common-cause fork. Connected means a graph does not imply independence, not that dependence has been measured.

svg.text: CausalLab | d-separation makes graph assumptions inspectable
Ancestor restriction -> moralize -> remove conditioned nodes -> connectivity. No probabilities or data fitting.
Right column: moral witness or no remaining route.
Right column: moral witness or no remaining route.
X / Y is a moral-graph witness via coparent bridge at C.
do(X): dashed U -> X is removed, not conditioned on.
Surgery happens before finding ancestors or moralizing.
Separated => conditional independence for distributions Markov to the supplied DAG.
Connected does not assert dependence. Include latent common causes; deterministic effects can add independences.
Witnesses belong to the ancestral moral graph, not necessarily to original-DAG active paths. No graph learning.
Fixed motifs, eight full query traces and graph hashes are embedded in this SVG. No graph or parameter search.
